techniques: Review the deduplication key/criteria for correlation with protected attributes before dropping records.
Apply deduplication within each demographic subgroup rather than against the full dataset, to avoid one group absorbing most of the drop.

references.citation: Wu, N., Vatsalan, D., Verma, S., & Kaafar, M.A. (2022). Fairness and Cost Constrained Privacy-Aware Record Linkage. IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security, 17, 2644-2656.

techniques: Implement group-stratified imputation instead of a single global fill value.
Check whether the missingness rate itself differs by subgroup before choosing an imputation strategy - missingness that correlates with a protected attribute is itself a bias signal.

references.citation: Khan, F.A., Herasymuk, D., Protsiv, N., & Stoyanovich, J. (2024). Still More Shades of Null: An Evaluation Suite for Responsible Missing Value Imputation. Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment.

techniques: Compute outlier bounds (z-score / IQR) per subgroup rather than one global threshold.
Sample and manually review a batch of records flagged as outliers from the affected subgroup before removal.

references.citation: Deepak, P. & Abraham, S.S. (2020/2021). FairLOF: Fairness in Outlier Detection. Data Science and Engineering.
Shekhar, S., Shah, N., & Akoglu, L. (2021). FairOD: Fairness-aware Outlier Detection.

techniques: Re-evaluate rare-category grouping/encoding choices - one-hot encoding has been shown to carry more direct group discrimination than regularized target encoding in some settings, while raw target encoding can leak label information.
Watch for intersectional cardinality effects: combining protected attributes into one high-cardinality feature can worsen discrimination even when each attribute alone looked fine.

references.citation: Mougan, C., Alvarez, J.M., Ruggieri, S., & Staab, S. (2022). Fairness Implications of Encoding Protected Categorical Attributes.

techniques: Verify the balancing target (e.g., SMOTE) includes the intersectional subgroup, not just the primary class label - balancing on outcome alone can leave a demographic subgroup still underrepresented.

Compare subgroup-level fairness metrics (not just accuracy) before and after resampling - oversampling improves class balance but does not automatically improve fairness metrics like average odds difference.

references.citation: Kabir, M.A., Ahmed, M.U., Begum, S., Barua, S., & Islam, M.R. (2024). Balancing Fairness: Unveiling the Potential of SMOTE-Driven Oversampling in AI Model Enhancement.
Dablain, D., Krawczyk, B., & Chawla, N.V. (2022). Towards A Holistic View of Bias in Machine Learning: Bridging Algorithmic Fairness and Imbalanced Learning.

techniques: Use per-group normalization or robust scaling if subgroup value distributions differ substantially from the global distribution.

references.citation: Feldman, M., Friedler, S.A., Moeller, J., Scheidegger, C., & Venkatasubramanian, S. (2015). Certifying and Removing Disparate Impact. ACM SIGKDD.

techniques: Consider reweighing records so each demographic combination contributes proportionally to model training, without deleting or relabeling any data.
Consider a fair representation learning step upstream, which encodes the data while obscuring protected-attribute membership.
